person_made_it: Trent's own edition: his name, his colour, his half of the duel, his hello line, and the circuit explained as three circles and two bands with a legend, because he is the quiet one who wants the day exact, not loud; the numbers are the real Friday qualifying and standings, spoiler-free.
emcee_who_is_speaking: The legend has the mic: each shape names one fact, the black circle is the Old City, the vermilion circle is the 57 percent, the short red band is the 0.837; Darby speaks only in the audio; Gordon closes with the challenge.
what_time_of_day_is_this_room: Saturday afternoon on paper: cream ground, black, vermilion and ochre, the Tanaka idiom of a physical setup explained by geometry, deliberately the one light page of the three so the trio can be judged by contrast.
did_the_click_pay_me: Confirming as Trent plays his voice line, the countdown sits under the audio as a plate, picks lock on the phone, the couch illustration is framed in black rule, and the game link starts the race where he takes the right half.
works_for_the_recipient: Zen Kaku Gothic New from Google Fonts with a system fallback, the geometry is pure CSS so it renders with scripts off, the tables carry the same numbers as the other two editions, and the light page uses color-scheme light so controls do not paint dark.
taught_me_something: Reducing the circuit to shapes made one thing obvious: the safety car is born inside the city walls, so the vermilion circle belongs inside the black one, and that is the whole strategy of the race in one picture.
told_me_the_truth: Verstappen's grid effect is marked unconfirmed, the strategy claim stops at what Formula 1 published, the geometry is labelled as explanation not a map, and the sources sit behind a spoiler warning.
weakest: It breaks the standing dark-room convention on purpose; if Gordon prefers all three dark, the cream flips to a deep ink ground with the same three colours in one edit.
